said:
Population and origins
All confirmed inhabitants are human. The differences are cultural: where someone grew up, how their community survived and who bore the costs of earlier expeditions.
| Community | Background | Possible tensions |
| Beltborn | Raised on stations and ships of the Lantern Belt. Accustomed to shared services and strict maintenance rules. | Some consider planetary residents careless with resources. |
| Nacreans | Local colonists and their descendants. Know the coast, storms and settlement history. | Some distrust researchers who leave as soon as their project is finished. |
| Transit Families | Families who have travelled between settlements for generations, transporting cargo, making repairs and trading. | Their changing residence is sometimes wrongly taken for a lack of loyalty. |

Origin does not determine character or reliability. Distrust mainly arises from personal experience and conflicting interests.
The first six characters
These are the most important encounters during the first research phase. The remaining professional roles are filled later. All six have a small private cabin in the residents' wing of Guest Quarters; initially, those cabins are not separate playable locations.
| Person | Origin and belief | Work and regular locations | Attitude and interest |
| Mara Venn — Port Coordinator | Nacrean; follows The Keeping. | Arrival Lock during arrivals; administration and meals in Commons. | Your first encounter. Businesslike and helpful if you keep agreements. Wants the expedition to leave the colony sufficient supplies. |
| Dr Ilyan Sorell — Research Lead | Beltborn; sympathetic to The Open Sky. | Orison Listening Room on field days; Common Deck for analysis and meetings. | Your client. Curious, persuasive and impatient. Believes delay may mean losing a unique opportunity. |
| Tessa Rook — Chief Engineer | Transit Families; non-religious. | Workshop in the morning; Peregrine Hangar during tests. | Speaks briefly and precisely. Wants to know what you actually measured. Refuses to sign off on safety on the strength of enthusiasm. |
| Niko Serrin — Signal Technician | Nacrean; non-religious, but participates in remembrance. | Orison Listening Room during the day; returns via Ridge Shelter. | Found the anomalous recording. Observant, tired and afraid he will be blamed for a maintenance error. |
| Dr Edda Vale — Medic | Beltborn; follows The Keeping. | Medical Bay; usually present at the evening meal. | Calm and direct. Honestly explains the implant and the limits of recovery. Protects patient information, even from the research lead. |
| Sana Holt — Steward | Nacrean with relatives in the Transit Families; follows The Keeping. | Commons around meals; Guest Quarters during cleaning and stock work. | Remembers names and habits. Wants to keep the community together, but refuses to pass on every confidence as news. |

First encounter
Mara waits at Arrival Lock. She checks your contract, directs you to your bed and says Sorell expects you at the next meal. She immediately offers one practical piece of advice:
“Before you promise him anything, ask Tessa what it will cost.”
Sana then welcomes you in Commons. She names those present and explains where to find the others. The player does not have to sit through six introductions in a row.
Who distrusts whom and why
Mara distrusts Sorell's priorities. He previously requested emergency supplies for a test as though they were ordinary research stock. Mara blocked their issue.
Tessa doubts Sorell's safety margins. She respects his knowledge, but feels he too readily presents uncertainties as details that can be resolved.
Niko is cautious around Tessa. He installed an unofficial bypass in the antenna system to preserve measurements. He fears her reaction, although she considers honestly reported mistakes less serious than concealed ones.
Edda resists pressure from the research team. Medical fitness is her decision; an approaching departure does not change that.
Sana trusts Mara, but defends Niko. She sees that he sleeps badly. This does not mean she knows the technical cause of his worries.
None begins as a secret villain. Their disagreements must be understandable even without sabotage or alien influence.
Law and authority
Port Vesper falls under the Vesper Settlement Compact, a local agreement within the Belt Charter.
Mara is also Settlement Marshal. She controls access, investigates complaints and can take temporary measures. The harbour watch on duty assists with incidents and emergencies. Serious cases are decided at a hearing by three uninvolved residents; anyone personally involved does not participate.
The rules apply in Port Vesper, Vesper Works and Orison Ridge. During an expedition, the appointed captain exercises authority aboard ship. The research lead is not automatically the captain.
| Offence | Usual consequence |
| A first minor offence, such as causing a nuisance or unauthorised but harmless passage | Warning and explanation; repeated offences generally 5–15 credits. |
| Taking tools without permission, limited damage or repeatedly ignoring access rules | Return the item or repair the damage, plus 20–60 credits; possibly temporary loss of access. |
| Theft of valuable equipment or deliberate damage to research data | Return or restoration, generally 60–200 credits, loss of privileges and a formal review. |
| Violence causing serious injury, deliberate sabotage of life support or opening an airlock while endangering people | Immediate intervention, temporary secure custody and a formal hearing. Possible removal from a role and transfer to an authorised Charter port. |
| Murder or deliberately endangering lives on a large scale | No fine that buys release; formal prosecution and secure transport as soon as responsibly possible. |

There is no death penalty, and nobody is put outside without protection as punishment. Debt can be repaid through agreed work, but emergency care remains available.
Suspicion is not evidence. An owner may notice something missing without knowing who took it. Witnesses, access records and physical traces have limited reach. The AI must not establish guilt merely because the player happened to be nearby.
Groups the player can join
| Group | Joining | What you receive and what is expected |
| Vesper Maintenance Cooperative | Safety instruction, one supervised job and approval by an authorised member, initially Tessa. | Borrowing tools, workshop use and paid jobs. Return borrowed equipment and report mistakes. |
| Peregrine Expedition Crew | Complete the first investigation, give informed consent to the risks and receive an appropriate task and training. | Access to relevant ship compartments, expedition equipment and a separate contract. No unrestricted access to every system. |
| The Keeping Circle | Voluntarily help with a meal, a vigil or maintaining the Harbour Record. A profession of faith is not required. | Social contacts, practical support and shared memories. Handle confidential stories according to the wishes of those involved. |

Memberships can overlap. Nobody has to join a religious group to complete the main assignment.
What people talk about
A story everyone knows The Night of the Open Door
Seventeen years ago, a maintenance team became stranded during a winter storm. A steward kept the outer reception module accessible after a sensor incorrectly reported that everyone was inside. The three people left behind eventually reached the port.
The event is recorded in the Harbour Record. There are different versions of who first noticed people were missing. The expression “Count the people, not the lights” is a reminder that a system notification does not replace a human being.
A concrete worry winter supplies
The same spare parts are needed for the Peregrine and the settlement's heating and water systems. Stocks are limited; the forecast storm may delay the next delivery.
Mara wants to keep supplies separate. Tessa looks for substitute parts. Sorell wants to show that the ship needs less than feared. The player can examine the inventory, help repair things or arrange an alternative.
A rumour an answer before the question
During a late meal, Niko said part of the signal resembled a test pattern which, according to the logged times, the Peregrine transmitted only later.
What is actually established:
The recordings exist.
There is a match between two patterns.
The clocks of the listening station and the test installation were not demonstrably synchronised.
Some residents now say the ship “has already been somewhere”. Others suspect a measurement error or manipulation. None of these explanations is proven at the start.
For the Chronicler
Give each character their own observations, limited knowledge and a reason to tell or withhold something. Connect new rumours to a source. Establish the signal's hidden explanation separately before creating further clues.
Let familiarity grow through shared work and agreements. After a few days, the player should be able to say: Mara keeps the village running, Tessa wants evidence, Niko has seen something — and I understand why they do not entirely trust one another.
